title: Java Inner Classes
learningObjectives: Define an inner class as a class declared inside another class.
Create an instance of a non-static inner class through an outer object.
Explain how an inner class can access members of its enclosing class.
Distinguish a non-static inner class from a static nested class.
Choose nested types when they are closely related to their enclosing type.

understand.concept: A nested class is declared inside another class. A non-static nested class is called an inner class and is associated with an instance of the outer class. A static nested class does not require an outer object instance.
understand.whyItMatters: Nested types keep helper types close to the class they support and can express a strong logical relationship. They should be used when their scope and purpose are genuinely tied to the enclosing type.
understand.analogy: Think of a well-designed object as a small service with a clear responsibility: it keeps the information it owns and exposes only the operations other code needs.
understand.analogyLimit: This analogy is only a design aid; Java access, inheritance and dispatch follow the language's exact rules.

explain.narrative:
## Non-static inner classes

Declare a class inside another class without static. Create it using an outer object, such as `outer.new Inner()`. An inner class can access members of its enclosing instance, including private members.

## Static nested classes

A nested class declared static does not carry an enclosing instance reference. It can directly access only static members of the outer class unless it receives an outer object.

## Local and anonymous classes

Java also supports classes declared within a block and anonymous class expressions. Use them when a short-lived implementation belongs near its use.

## Common mistakes

- Trying to instantiate a non-static inner class without an outer instance.
- Treating a static nested class as if it had an enclosing object automatically.
- Nesting classes without a clear relationship.

examples.title: Create a non-static inner class
examples.code:
class Outer { class Inner { void show() { System.out.println("Inside"); } } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Outer outer = new Outer(); Outer.Inner inner = outer.new Inner(); inner.show(); } }
examples.explanation: A non-static inner object is created through an outer instance.

examples.title: Inner class accesses outer field
examples.code:
class House { private String address = "North"; class Room { void show() { System.out.println(address); } } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { House h = new House(); h.new Room().show(); } }
examples.explanation: The inner class can access private members of its enclosing instance.

examples.title: Static nested class
examples.code:
class Computer { static class Chip { void info() { System.out.println("Chip"); } } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Computer.Chip chip = new Computer.Chip(); chip.info(); } }
examples.explanation: A static nested class can be instantiated without a Computer object.

examples.title: Two outer instances have distinct inner access
examples.code:
class Box { String label; Box(String label) { this.label = label; } class Tag { void print() { System.out.println(label); } } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Box a = new Box("A"); Box b = new Box("B"); a.new Tag().print(); b.new Tag().print(); } }
examples.explanation: Each inner object is associated with its particular outer instance.

examples.title: Nested type groups helper behaviour
examples.code:
class Order { static class Status { static String current() { return "Pending"; } } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println(Order.Status.current()); } }
examples.explanation: The nested type keeps a related status helper within Order's namespace.

questions.prompt: Where is an inner class declared?
questions.explanation: An inner class is a non-static nested class.

questions.prompt: How do you create a non-static inner class object?
questions.answer: Through an outer object using outer.new Inner()
options: Through an outer object using outer.new Inner()
questions.explanation: A non-static inner class is associated with an enclosing object.

questions.prompt: Can an inner class access private members of its enclosing class?
questions.explanation: Nested classes have access to members of their enclosing class.

questions.prompt: Does a static nested class require an outer object?
questions.explanation: A static nested class has no implicit enclosing instance.

questions.prompt: When is a nested class useful?
questions.answer: When a helper type is closely related to its enclosing type
options: When a helper type is closely related to its enclosing type
Whenever a class has more than one method
questions.explanation: Nested types can keep tightly related implementation details together.
